Vivek / Marissa —

I've reviewed the questionnaire and compiled a redline for the order form. High-level positions and reasoning below:

- IP: We cannot accept broad assignment of output IP where Catalyst provides training data. Proposed compromise: Redwood grants Catalyst an exclusive (or perpetual, non-exclusive depending on deal level) right to use and sublicense outputs that are solely derived from Catalyst's proprietary data, but Redwood retains model improvements (weights/derivative model enhancements). We add a narrow data-to-output carve-out and a mutual cooperation clause for patent prosecution.

- Indemnity: We will accept indemnity for claims arising from Redwood's grossly negligent handling of Catalyst's data or proven willful misconduct. We cannot indemnify for all third-party claims arising from customer-provided content. For third-party claims about generated outputs (e.g., alleged IP infringement), propose a limited mutual indemnity with procedure (notice, defense control thresholds, and settlement consent).

- Liability Cap: Our standard is a cap equal to 12 months of fees for the impacted service, subject to exclusions (IP breach, gross negligence) where higher caps survive. For strategic enterprise deals we can consider higher caps (e.g., 24 months) with an enterprise commercial uplift/insurance proof. Recommend a tiered approach in the order form: Hosted subscription fees cap = 12 months; data-breach or IP-specific exceptions reserved.

- Order form practicals: Include a schedule listing the model variants and hosting location (US region) to limit export/data residency issues. Add a data handling addendum (logging, KMS, retention) as a referenced exhibit.

I've attached redline: redline_order_form_v2.docx and a marked-up questionnaire with Q/A entries. I'm leaving placeholders for commercial values (fees/month) which Marissa should fill.

Attachment: redline_order_form_v2.docx (docx)

Hi Andrew —

Appreciate the quick turnaround request. Please find attached our consolidated Q&A and a redlined order form addressing the questions Catalyst flagged. Summary of the principal points: 

1) IP & outputs: Redwood will not take assignment of Catalyst-provided data. We will grant Catalyst rights to outputs that are derived solely from their proprietary data (see Q9 in attached PDF). Redwood retains improvements to models and internal weights.

2) Indemnity & third-party claims: Redwood accepts indemnity for claims arising from our gross negligence or willful misconduct. For third-party infringement claims tied to generated outputs, we propose a limited mutual indemnity with the standard defense-notice-and-consent process.

3) Liability cap: We propose a cap equal to 18 months of subscription/consumption fees for the agreement. As a commercial compromise, if Catalyst requires 12 months we can agree subject to a one-time platform support fee and updated SLAs. There are standard carve-outs for willful misconduct and IP-specific claims.

4) Data handling & exhibits: The redline includes references to an exhibit for data processing, retention, and KMS controls; we confirm hosting in the US region for this deployment.

Documents attached: Redwood_Response_Catalyst_RFP_20261220.pdf (pdf, 19 pages) and OrderForm_Redwood_Catalyst_20261220.docx (docx, redline).
